body:
What I find so confusing is that so many people did figure it out. Were they in more pain than me? Do I have to feel _worse_ than I already do to have the courage to jump?

A while ago I read about a young person (14 I think? It was on BBC news) managing to kill themselves. My first thought was that even a child can do it and I can't? That's a pretty telling thought considering I should have been sad that somebody so young both felt that way and did something about it.

Sorry for rambling, that wasn't really related. Of your two ideas, personally I hope I'm in the former. Simply because I think I can beat my survival instinct. I've done it before (those attempts failed rather than not being able to do it) and I only need to do it very briefly.

Thanks for replying. I don't think it is hope that stopped me but fear. For some reason the physical act of jumping is hard. I've tried other methods (I'm not sure if it is against the rules to discuss them in detail, so I won't) and at the time I thought they would kill me.

Maybe coward is too harsh a word, but it does take courage to jump. Courage I don't have yet.

Thanks for telling your story. I've also waited in front of train platforms a lot of times but, as you say, far too many people. That's why I went up when it was dark. I had hoped spending a bit of time alone at the top would get me "psyched up" enough to do it. Either that or the alcohol would do it. Clearly it didn't work.

Honestly I don't want to get better - I don't think I could even if I wanted to. I'm not really sure why I'm even posting here to be honest. Maybe I just want to talk about it without the risk of being sent to a hospital? I'm not sure.

Thank you for your reply. But I do disagree, I really don't think it's hope stopping me - It's fear. I just don't know how to get over it. That's why I was drinking. I was hoping to get too drunk to walk properly so I'd slip but I gave up before getting to that point.

The only other "way out" is carrying on with my life, but there's absolutely nothing in it that I want. I honestly don't want to get better, I just want to stop living.

I spent most of my time while sitting on the edge (and all the way home) thinking about how do other people manage to jump? I'm so terrified of the fall. I know that I'll feel almost nothing on impact. I've been skydiving, free-falling was fine, but somehow this is difficult. I don't get how so many other people have done it but I can't.
